overall_strategy: Because you're in Journey Month 1-2 with Coci (a 5-year-old, 50 lb Shar Pei living in an apartment with no yard and a documented chicken allergy), the priority is to cover daily consumables reliably (chicken-free food, training treats, waste bags, wipes, dental chews, and enzyme cleaner) on autoship so you never run out, while also supplying essential one-time setup and enrichment items now (water fountain, cooling mat due to heat warnings, harness, slow-feeder, bed, grooming tools, and durable toys). Subscriptions lean on realistic depletion math (food: ~3.5 cups/day → 105 cups/month; choose bag sizes and cadences that match storage and feeding preferences). Many grooming/medical topical items (wipes, ear solution, paw balm, dental chews) are set to longer or flexible autoship cadences so you get convenience without overshipping. One-time purchases focus on safety, comfort, and enrichment that last months to years — items that set Coci up for success in apartment life and address seasonal risks (cooling pad, fountain) or training/behavior support (harness, ThunderShirt, snuffle mat).
